def find_max_hamming_distance(n, arr):
    # The maximum Hamming distance is achieved by placing the two unique elements of A
    # as far apart as possible in B. Since the frequency of each element is at most 2,
    # we can always achieve a Hamming distance of N-1 by placing one element at the
    # beginning and the other at the end of B.
    unique_elements = sorted(set(arr))
    b = [0] * n
    b[0], b[-1] = unique_elements[0], unique_elements[1]
    return b

def main():
    t = int(input())
    for _ in range(t):
        n = int(input())
        arr = list(map(int, input().split()))
        
        # Find the maximum possible Hamming distance
        max_hamming_distance = n - 1
        print(max_hamming_distance)
        
        # Generate the array B
        b = find_max_hamming_distance(n, arr)
        print(*b)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
